fields.System.Title: EPIC FDN — Foundation and Platform
fields.System.Description:
Goal

The service starts, knows who is calling, records what they did, and holds the reference data
that everything else points at.

Business value

Nothing else can be built without this. More importantly, three things here are extremely
expensive to retrofit: authentication, audit, and correct master data identity. Getting them
right in week one costs days. Getting them wrong costs months.

Scope

In. Service skeleton, configuration, logging, error handling, database and migrations,
users and permissions, audit trail, products, locations, zones, units of measure, partners,
reason codes, the event outbox.

Out. Any warehouse behaviour. This epic holds no business rules about stock — it holds the
things stock rules will need.

Done when

  • One command starts the API and database, and the seed warehouse loads.
  • An unauthenticated request is rejected; an authorised one succeeds.
  • Every write is attributed to a user or API client in the audit log.
  • A product and a location can be created, bulk imported, and blocked.
  • Migrations run forward and backward cleanly.
  • Events written to the outbox are delivered by a worker and retried on failure.

Key risks

| Risk | Why it matters | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| SKU used as a technical key | Everything breaks at once on a catalogue renumber | [doc 03 §7.2](../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Nullable fields the algorithms require | Putaway makes nonsense suggestions | [doc 03 §7.4](../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Duplicate products | Stock splits; both look low | [doc 03 §7.5](../../docs/03-master-data.md) |
| Partial bulk import | Half a catalogue, unclear which half | [doc 09 §11.4](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Permission checks scattered across routes | One endpoint gets missed | [doc 04 §3.1](../../docs/04-modules.md) |
| Audit table growth | A full scan takes the database down by month six | [doc 04 §3.1](../../docs/04-modules.md) |
